title: Ranking Ties Three Ways
focus: Drill how ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK diverge on a leaderboard containing tied scores, showing that only RANK leaves gaps in the sequence and only ROW_NUMBER is non-deterministic unless the ORDER BY breaks ties on a unique column.

title: Day-over-Day Revenue Change with LAG
focus: Drill computing the absolute and percentage change from the previous day with LAG, including what the first row of every partition returns and why a NULL default silently swallows the first period.

title: Time to Next Order with LEAD
focus: Drill using LEAD partitioned by customer to measure the gap in days until each customer's next order, and handling the trailing row where no next order exists.

title: Running Total and the RANGE-versus-ROWS Peer Trap
focus: Drill a cumulative revenue total with SUM OVER, exposing that the default RANGE frame lumps all rows sharing an ORDER BY value into one peer group so same-day rows all show the day-end total instead of a row-by-row cumulative.

title: Seven-Day Moving Average of Signups
focus: Drill a trailing seven-row moving average with an explicit ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING frame, and decide what the first six rows should report when the window is not yet full.

title: Share of Category Total and Quartile Buckets
focus: Drill emitting a per-row percentage of its category total using an aggregate window function that does not collapse rows, then bucketing the same rows into quartiles with NTILE in a single pass.

title: Employees and Their Managers
focus: Drill a self-join of an employee table onto itself on manager_id so every employee shows their manager's name, and why an INNER JOIN silently drops the top-level employee whose manager_id is NULL.

title: Customers Who Never Ordered
focus: Drill the three equivalent spellings of an anti-join -- LEFT JOIN with an IS NULL filter, NOT EXISTS, and EXCEPT -- and why the IS NULL predicate must sit in the WHERE clause rather than the ON clause.

title: The NOT IN NULL Trap
focus: Drill why NOT IN against a subquery whose column contains even one NULL returns zero rows under three-valued logic, and how NOT EXISTS gives the intended answer unchanged.

title: Join Fan-Out Double Counting
focus: Drill an order total that is silently inflated because the order row is joined to both line items and payments at once, and fix it by pre-aggregating each child table to one row per order before joining.

title: Overlapping Bookings on the Same Room
focus: Drill an inequality self-join that finds every pair of bookings on the same room whose date intervals overlap, using the start-before-other-end and end-after-other-start condition and an id comparison to avoid reporting each pair twice.

title: Latest Order per Customer with LATERAL
focus: Drill a correlated LATERAL join that fetches each customer's most recent order row, and contrast it with the window-function and correlated-subquery formulations on both readability and access pattern.
skip_exec_reason: SQLite has no LATERAL (or CROSS APPLY) join syntax, so the correlated subquery in the FROM clause is a parse error.

title: Categories Above a Sales Threshold
focus: Drill filtering groups on an aggregate with HAVING while a row-level predicate stays in WHERE, and show how moving one predicate between the two clauses changes the result.

title: Counting Rows, Values and Distinct Values
focus: Drill the difference between COUNT(*), COUNT(column) and COUNT(DISTINCT column) on a table with NULLs and repeats, and why AVG over a nullable column divides by the non-NULL count rather than the row count.

title: Pivoting Monthly Revenue into Columns
focus: Drill turning one row per month into one column per month with SUM(CASE WHEN ...) conditional aggregation, plus the FILTER (WHERE ...) spelling, and note why a pivot with an unknown column set needs generated SQL.

title: Median Without a Builtin
focus: Drill computing an exact median from row counts and ordinal positions when no MEDIAN function exists, correctly averaging the two middle values on an even row count and per group rather than overall.

title: Ninety-Fifth Percentile Latency by Endpoint
focus: Drill computing a p95 latency per endpoint without PERCENTILE_CONT, choosing explicitly between the nearest-rank definition and linear interpolation between neighbouring order statistics and showing they disagree on small samples.

title: Subtotals and Grand Totals in One Result Set
focus: Drill producing region, region-plus-product and grand-total rows from one scan with ROLLUP or GROUPING SETS, and using GROUPING() to tell a real NULL apart from a subtotal placeholder.
skip_exec_reason: SQLite implements neither GROUPING SETS/ROLLUP/CUBE nor the GROUPING() function, so the grouping clause fails to parse.

title: Refactoring Nested Subqueries into CTEs
focus: Drill rewriting a triple-nested inline-view query as a chain of named non-recursive CTEs that each do one step, keeping the result identical while making the aggregation order explicit.

title: Generating a Complete Date Spine
focus: Drill building a contiguous calendar of dates with a recursive CTE and left-joining sparse event data onto it so days with zero events appear as zero rather than vanishing from the report.

title: Walking the Org Chart
focus: Drill a recursive CTE that walks a manager hierarchy from a given root, carrying a depth counter and an accumulated path string, and distinguishing UNION from UNION ALL in the recursive term.

title: Consecutive Login Streaks
focus: Drill the gaps-and-islands date-minus-row-number trick to collapse consecutive daily logins into islands and report each user's longest streak, including the deduplication needed when a user logs in twice a day.

title: Collapsing Overlapping Date Ranges
focus: Drill merging overlapping and adjacent subscription intervals per customer into minimal disjoint ranges by starting a new island whenever a row's start exceeds the running maximum end date of all prior rows.

title: Cycle-Safe Reachability in a Graph
focus: Drill a recursive CTE over a directed edge table that finds every node reachable from a start node while carrying a visited-path string to break cycles that would otherwise make the recursion never terminate.

title: Bucketing Events into Days, Weeks and Months
focus: Drill truncating timestamps into day, ISO-week and month buckets with date functions, and why grouping on a formatted string sorts correctly only when the format is zero-padded and year-first.

title: Monthly Cohort Retention Matrix
focus: Drill assembling a retention matrix that groups users by their first-purchase month and counts, for each subsequent month offset, how many of that cohort were active, with the cohort size as the denominator throughout.

title: Funnel Conversion Rates by Step
focus: Drill counting distinct users reaching each funnel step and reporting both overall and step-to-step conversion rates, ensuring counts are monotonically non-increasing because a later step implies the earlier one.

title: Funnel Steps That Must Happen In Order
focus: Drill an order-preserving funnel where each step only counts if its timestamp is strictly after the previous step's, and show how the naive per-step EXISTS version overcounts users who did the steps out of sequence.

title: Sessionizing Clickstream with a 30-Minute Timeout
focus: Drill splitting a per-user event stream into sessions by flagging every event whose gap from the previous event exceeds a thirty-minute inactivity threshold and turning a running sum of those flags into a session identifier.

title: Week-over-Week Growth on a Gap-Free Calendar
focus: Drill week-over-week growth where weeks with no activity must appear as zero, so the comparison uses a gap-free week series rather than LAG over only the weeks that happen to have rows.

title: Top Three Products per Category
focus: Drill top-N per group with a partitioned ROW_NUMBER filtered in an outer query, and decide when RANK is the right choice instead because tied Nth-place rows must all be kept.

title: Deleting Exact Duplicate Rows
focus: Drill removing exact duplicate rows from a table with no primary key by numbering rows within each duplicate group and keeping only the first, and why a plain SELECT DISTINCT does not solve the deletion.

title: Collapsing Near-Duplicate Customer Records
focus: Drill collapsing near-duplicate contacts that differ only by casing, whitespace and punctuation by grouping on a normalized match key, then picking a surviving record with an explicit tie-break on completeness and recency.

title: Building a Type-2 Slowly Changing Dimension
focus: Drill turning a stream of dimension snapshots into SCD type 2 rows with valid_from, valid_to and is_current, closing each version with the next change's timestamp and emitting a new version only when a tracked attribute actually changed.

title: Latest Row per Key with QUALIFY
focus: Drill filtering directly on a window function's result with QUALIFY to keep the newest row per key, and contrast it with the portable subquery wrapper that every dialect requires.
skip_exec_reason: SQLite has no QUALIFY clause, so a window function cannot be filtered without wrapping the query in a subquery.

title: Reading a Query Plan and Choosing an Index
focus: Drill reading EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN to tell a full SCAN from an indexed SEARCH, choosing the leading column of a composite index for an equality-plus-range predicate, and recognizing that wrapping a column in a function makes the predicate non-sargable.

title: The Two Children Problem
focus: Drill how the answer changes between 'at least one child is a girl' and 'the older child is a girl' because the two statements condition on different subsets of the four equally likely sibling orderings.

title: The Rare Disease Screening Test
focus: Drill computing the positive predictive value of a highly sensitive screening test for a low-prevalence disease, showing that most positives are false positives because the base rate dominates the likelihood ratio.

title: Monty Hall, With Three Doors and With Ten
focus: Drill why switching wins two thirds of the time with three doors and generalizes to (n-1)/n when the host knowingly opens all but one remaining door, and how the answer collapses to a coin flip if the host opens doors at random.

title: Which Urn Did the Ball Come From
focus: Drill a one-step Bayes update on which of two differently composed urns produced an observed draw, working it both with the full formula and with prior odds times the likelihood ratio.

title: The Prosecutor's Fallacy
focus: Drill the difference between the probability of the evidence given innocence and the probability of innocence given the evidence, showing how a one-in-a-million match probability yields a far-from-certain guilt posterior once the suspect pool size is accounted for.

title: Two Screening Tests in Sequence
focus: Drill updating a disease posterior twice using the first test's posterior as the second test's prior, and how the answer changes when the two tests' errors are correlated rather than conditionally independent.

title: Expected Payout of a Dice Game
focus: Drill computing the expected payout of a strictly positive dice-based payout schedule directly from the probability mass function and again via linearity of expectation over indicator variables.

title: Variance of a Sum, Independent and Correlated
focus: Drill why the variance of a sum equals the sum of variances only under zero covariance, and quantify how much the covariance term shifts the total for a pair of positively correlated variables.

title: The Birthday Problem
focus: Drill the shared-birthday probability for a room of a given size using the complement of all-distinct birthdays, and explain why the crossover past one half arrives at a group size far smaller than intuition suggests.

title: Coupon Collector: Completing the Set
focus: Drill the expected number of draws to collect all n distinct coupons by decomposing the wait into independent geometric stages whose means form a harmonic sum.

title: Expected Maximum of n Uniform Draws
focus: Drill deriving the distribution of the maximum of n independent uniform draws from the CDF raised to the nth power, then integrating it to get the expected maximum and the expected minimum by symmetry.

title: Expected Rolls to See Three Sixes in a Row
focus: Drill setting up and solving the system of first-step-analysis equations for the expected number of die rolls until three consecutive sixes appear, and why the answer is far larger than three times the wait for one six.

title: Stationary Distribution of a Two-State Chain
focus: Drill solving the balance equations of a two-state weather chain for its stationary distribution and confirming that long-run occupancy is independent of the starting state for an irreducible aperiodic chain.

title: Gambler's Ruin
focus: Drill the probability that a gambler with a given bankroll reaches a target before going broke under a slightly unfavourable per-bet edge, using the standard difference-equation solution for a biased walk.

title: Expected Hitting Time on a Cycle
focus: Drill computing the expected number of steps for a symmetric random walk on a small cycle graph to first reach a designated node, by writing one first-step equation per state and solving the linear system.

title: Expected Steps to Absorption
focus: Drill computing expected time to absorption for a multi-state absorbing chain from the fundamental matrix of the transient submatrix, and reading off absorption probabilities for each absorbing state.

title: Waiting for HTH Versus HHT
focus: Drill why two equally likely three-flip patterns have different expected waiting times, tracing the state machine that shows a failed HTH attempt can reuse its suffix while a failed HHT attempt cannot.

title: Poisson Arrivals and Memorylessness
focus: Drill that the wait until the next arrival in a Poisson process is exponential with the same mean no matter how long you have already waited, and compute the probability of a given number of arrivals in a fixed window.

title: Which Distribution Models This Scenario
focus: Drill matching each of several described data-generating scenarios to binomial, Poisson, geometric, exponential or negative binomial, and stating the specific assumption that would make the obvious choice wrong.

title: Maximum Likelihood for an Exponential Rate
focus: Drill deriving the maximum likelihood estimator of an exponential rate by writing the log-likelihood, differentiating, solving the score equation and confirming the second derivative makes it a maximum.

title: Maximum Likelihood for a Uniform Upper Bound
focus: Drill why the MLE for the upper endpoint of a uniform distribution is the sample maximum rather than a stationary point of the derivative, and quantify the downward bias that the unbiased correction removes.

title: Coverage of a Wald Interval for a Proportion
focus: Drill the actual coverage of a nominal 95 percent Wald interval for a small proportion at a modest sample size, showing it falls well short of 95 percent and that the Wilson interval repairs it.

title: Normal Versus t Interval for a Small Sample
focus: Drill constructing a confidence interval for a mean from a small sample with unknown variance, and quantify how much narrower and how wrong the interval becomes if the normal critical value is used instead of the t.

title: Sampling Distribution of the Sample Variance
focus: Drill why dividing the sum of squared deviations by n underestimates the population variance while dividing by n minus one is unbiased, and connect the scaled sample variance to a chi-square distribution.

title: Choosing the Right Test
topics: t vs chi-square vs Mann-Whitney selection
focus: Drill matching each described comparison to a two-sample t test, a paired t test, a chi-square test of independence or a Mann-Whitney U test, and naming the assumption violation that rules out each alternative.

title: What a p-Value Does Not Say
focus: Drill dismantling the standard misreadings of a p-value -- that it is the probability the null is true, that a large p-value proves no effect, and that significance implies a practically meaningful effect.

title: Sizing an A/B Test for a Two-Point Lift
focus: Drill computing the per-arm sample size needed to detect a two-percentage-point lift on a given baseline conversion rate at 80 percent power and a two-sided 5 percent level, and how the requirement scales as the effect shrinks.

title: Power of an Underpowered Experiment
focus: Drill computing the true power of a test that is run at a sample size far below what the target effect requires, and interpreting what a non-significant result from such a test does and does not license.

title: Peeking and Inflated Type I Error
focus: Drill how repeatedly checking an A/B test and stopping the moment p drops below 0.05 pushes the false-positive rate far above the nominal level even when the two arms are identical.

title: Chi-Square Test of Independence by Hand
topics: t vs chi-square vs Mann-Whitney selection
focus: Drill computing expected cell counts from the row and column marginals of a contingency table, forming the chi-square statistic and its degrees of freedom, and stating the minimum-expected-count condition for validity.

title: Simpson's Paradox in Treatment Success Rates
focus: Drill a treatment that wins within every severity stratum yet loses in the pooled table, and identify the unequal allocation across strata as the confounder that flips the sign on aggregation.

title: Regression to the Mean in Repeat Testing
focus: Drill the expected second-round score of candidates selected for scoring extremely high on the first round, and why the apparent decline is a property of noisy measurement rather than evidence that an intervention failed.

title: Survivorship Bias and the Returning Bombers
focus: Drill why armouring the parts of returning aircraft that show the most bullet holes is exactly backwards, and generalize the pattern to fund performance tables and startup advice drawn only from winners.

title: Length-Biased Sampling and the Inspection Paradox
focus: Drill why a passenger arriving at a random time waits longer than half the mean headway, because sampling an interval by landing inside it weights each interval by its own length.

title: Fermi Estimate of Peak Query Volume
focus: Drill decomposing peak queries per second for a consumer service into population, adoption rate, sessions per user per day and a peak-to-average multiplier, and stating which assumption the estimate is most sensitive to.

title: Berkson's Paradox and Collider Bias
focus: Drill how conditioning on an admission rule that accepts anyone strong on either of two independent traits induces a negative correlation between those traits inside the admitted group.
